step 1: claim the host
step 2: create /etc/paisans

step 4: record what admit installs
step 5: skip the mesh until its conf exists
step 6: start paisans-f2a9's manager after the mesh
step 7: delegate cgroups to users

step 10: load the egress table

step 11: load br_netfilter
  daemon: load br_netfilter now, which the user's daemon needs with its userland proxy off
  run:
    $ modprobe br_netfilter

step 12: load br_netfilter at boot
  daemon: list br_netfilter and nf_tables in /etc/modules-load.d/paisans.conf, shared by every admitted deployment
  write /etc/modules-load.d/paisans.conf mode 0644:
    | # Written by paisans site admit. The rootless Docker daemons of admitted
    | # deployments need br_netfilter to start with their userland proxy off,
    | # and the module their iptables uses for the setup tool to install them.
    | br_netfilter
    | nf_tables

step 13: write paisans-f2a9's daemon.json
step 14: install paisans-f2a9's rootless Docker
step 15: create /srv/paisans

step 17: create /etc/wireguard

step 20: install the helper's sudoers line
step 21: allow 22/tcp
step 22: allow 51820/udp
step 23: allow all inbound on psns-f2a9
step 24: set the host's sysctls

warning: delegation reaches paisans-f2a9's manager at its next start
  Its manager is running, and restarting it would restart its Docker daemon and every container in it, so admit does not. cpuset and io limits apply after the host's next reboot.
warning: br_netfilter: traffic over virbr0 passes the FORWARD chain from now on
  The chain's policy is DROP. --bridge-netfilter was given, and is recorded.
warning: forwarding: this turns on routing between every interface on this host
  The site has an endpoint, so it relays mesh traffic between sites behind NAT, which cannot dial each other. The firewall's forward policy governs what is routed.
